text:
Priya Kapoor: Heads-up — post-launch backlog needs a quick decision: which items go into a focused hotfix sprint vs. the regular enhancement backlog. Can we agree on criteria and owners today?
Alex Morgan: +1. Need to know eng capacity before we lock anything. What's the hotfix window?
Priya Kapoor: Thinking next Tue-Wed (48h window) for a small hotfix sprint (branch, test, canary -> GA). If that works, we'll triage by EOD today.
Marco Li: To clarify the buckets: Hotfix = customer-facing regressions or severe performance/availability issues that affect core flows. Enhancements = UX polish, non-blocking improvements, feature requests.
Jenna Shaw: Also add infra deploy risk: if a fix requires DB migration or infra changes, prefer scheduled minor release, unless it's Sev1. We should not do risky infra in the 48h hotfix.
Sam Reyes: From support: top-10 errors since launch (link to dashboard) — 4 are high-frequency but 2 are cosmetic. I'll drop a short list in the ticket.
Casey Dunn: Design note — some "looks broken" things are high-impact for new users. They feel like bugs, but may be quick CSS fixes that are safe for hotfix. We'll mark those as "UI-critical".
Priya Kapoor: Proposed triage rubric (short):
- Sev1/hotfix: prevents usage for >5% of active flows OR causes data loss OR blocks key customers.
- Sev2/next minor: major degradation <5% or big customer annoyance with workaround.
- Enhancement: feature requests, small UX improvements, perf tweaks under thresholds.
If it meets Sev1 -> assign to hotfix. Otherwise assign and schedule flow.
Marco Li: Can we automate initial tagging? triage-bot can tag `hotfix-candidate` if error-rate > X and linked to recent deploy.
triage-bot: I can run nightly checks and add `hotfix-candidate` to GH issues. Will post a list at 09:00 PT.
Alex Morgan: Capacity note: for a 48h hotfix window we can take ~3 medium fixes (or 1 big + 1 medium). Please prioritize accordingly.
Lauren Patel: Ops/process: freeze merges to `main` 12h before canary, and require `hotfix` label + owner. I'll update the release checklist.
Priya Kapoor: Ownership proposals: Alex -> eng lead for hotfix, Jenna -> rollout & monitoring, Sam -> customer comms, Lauren -> release ops. Casey will approve UI quick fixes. Marco helps triage automation.
Jenna Shaw: For monitoring, we'll ensure canary has 10% traffic and watch error-rate, latency P50/P95 and memory. Rollback plan ready: `rollback-to=release-1.0.0`.
Sam Reyes: I'll draft the support banner templates and a short message for customers affected. Can we use the support channel with a pinned status update?
Casey Dunn: I'll label UI fixes with `design-quick` if under 2hrs. Those are greenlights for hotfix if they meet impact criteria.
Priya Kapoor: Scheduling milestone names: `hotfix/1.0.1` for the urgent set; `next-wave/1.1` for the enhancement batch. I'll create both milestones and link issues.
Marco Li: One more ask: try to batch similar fixes together to minimize deploy churn. Use the `hotfix-bundle` tag if multiple related issues land together.
Alex Morgan: Agreed on bundling. Also want a short smoke test checklist in the GH PR template for hotfix -> `smoke: login, api happy path, embeddings`.
Priya Kapoor: OK — plan of action: 1) Sam posts top-10 and affected customers, 2) triage-bot runs and posts candidates, 3) team triages by EOD and adds `hotfix` label, 4) Lauren applies merge freeze and routes deploy checklist.
Lauren Patel: I'll post the freeze times and add `release-owner` in the checklist.
Sam Reyes: Posting the support list now.
Marco Li: I'll run a quick query: `gh issue list --label hotfix-candidate --json number,title,labels` and share results in #product after triage-bot posts.
Priya Kapoor: Thanks all — if nobody objects, we'll execute this cadence. Final check: any blockers?
Alex Morgan: No blockers from eng side.
Jenna Shaw: No from SRE. Ready to support canary monitoring.
Casey Dunn: No.
triage-bot: Done — nightly run scheduled; will emit candidates at 09:00 PT. :robot_face:
Priya Kapoor: Great — meeting at 16:00 today for final triage if needed. :thumbsup:
